about: Scenarios for `edakit sim`: two cell states x button pressed or released x the LED's forward-voltage corners, and a cell upside down. Cell data as in edakit's example coin-cell-led (handbook 17), with its sources.

fresh.note: off-load voltage of a fresh CR2032 at least 3.20 V (CR2032 specification, Farnell 1728774); internal resistance at most 20 Ohm fresh (Rayovac CR2032 S6600072 Issue E, 1 kHz, 10 mA pulse); at most 3 mA continuous, 15 mA in pulses (Jauch CR 2032 H2B technical data sheet, 15092025: Max. Continuous Current 3 mA, Max. Pulse Current 15 mA; Murata TCN-CR-002-E gives 20 mA for 2 s pulses and calls more than 10 mA a high drain with a large voltage drop) – the continuous value, a press of SW1 is no pulse of a defined length

used.note: Rayovac rates the capacity down to 2.5 V (220 mAh at 15 kOhm); 40 Ohm assumed – the internal resistance rises as the cell empties, no datasheet gives it; at most 3 mA continuous, 15 mA in pulses (Jauch CR 2032 H2B technical data sheet, 15092025: Max. Continuous Current 3 mA, Max. Pulse Current 15 mA; Murata TCN-CR-002-E gives 20 mA for 2 s pulses and calls more than 10 mA a high drain with a large voltage drop) – the continuous value, a press of SW1 is no pulse of a defined length

reversed.note: a fresh cell put in upside down – the holder takes it that way

pressed_reversed.about: SW1 held down with the cell upside down: D1 must stay dark

criteria_note: led_on_min_a 0.5 mA: D1 (LTST-C170KGKT, 18–71 mcd at 20 mA) gives about 0.03 × IV there by Fig. 4 of DS22-2000-073 Rev. H, 0.5–2 mcd – visibly lit on a desk indoors; edakit's default 1 mA is not reached by a D1 of the highest VF bin on a cell used down to 2.5 V (0.82 mA, D-4)
